Definition: of Chaldee origin (confidence, i.e. wealth, personified); mammonas, i.e. avarice (deified):--mammon.
BiblicalUsage: mammōnâs is mammon, wealth treated as a master. In Matthew 6:24 Jesus says no man can serve two masters, and that we cannot serve God and mammon, and Luke 16:13 repeats the warning. In Luke 16:9 He tells His hearers to make friends of the mammon of unrighteousness, using wealth for others before it fails, so the word is not money itself but money enthroned.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mammōnâs exposes the choice I make every day about who my master is, since wealth used for others is a tool and wealth served is a god, and I want no god but the LORD.
